hook_text: Strong and concentrated are NOT the same word — and mixing them up costs a mark almost every time acids appear.
clip_script: Strong acids like hydrochloric, sulfuric and nitric ionise completely; weak acids like ethanoic and oxalic ionise incompletely. Strong is about the FRACTION ionised, concentrated is about the AMOUNT dissolved — a dilute strong acid is entirely possible, and telling those words apart is a perennial mark.
visual_style: Two beakers side by side — one packed with fully split ions labelled 'strong', one crowded with intact molecules labelled 'concentrated' — swapping labels with a red buzzer until the correct pairing locks in green.
mood: Word-trap energy — two near-twins pulled apart in twenty seconds.
pacing: Quick label swaps with buzzer stings, a freeze on the correct pairing, then the 'dilute strong acid' reveal as the mic-drop.
call_to_action: Sweep the whole chemistry block — naming, equilibrium, acids and cells — in the full revision session.
